name: draggable-card

frames.best_why: Five tilted photo cards spread across the stage with the most labels readable and none cut at the edges.

tagline: Scattered polaroid-style photo cards you can drag and tilt.
summary: A set of tilted photo cards strewn across a dark stage; each tilts in 3D under the pointer, lifts on hover, and can be dragged around with momentum before settling.
appearance: Six dark cards with square landscape photos and a country name below sit at different angles across a black stage, showing mountains, coast, snow and forest. Their corners overlap and shadows separate them.
behaviour: Moving over a card tilts it toward the pointer and adds a faint white glare; dragging throws it in the direction of motion until a spring brings it to a stop and flattens the tilt.
demo_content: Photo cards labelled Canada, Namibia, Norway, Greece, Switzerland and a faint Fight Club quote.
search_phrases: photo cards you can drag around
polaroid style photos on a board
cards you can fling with momentum
card stack that tilts with the mouse
use_when: A hero or gallery wants a tactile, messy photo spread people can rearrange themselves.
avoid_when: Cards sit absolutely and overlap, so on small screens they collide and several labels are clipped.
customise: Wrap any children in a draggable body and position it with className; drag constraints, tilt range, spring and glare are fixed in the source.
weight_why: Six cards with springs and drag handlers; nothing animates while idle.

a11y.note: Cards can only be dragged with a pointer, with no keyboard movement and no reduced-motion handling.

issues: The Fight Club quote is dark grey on black and effectively invisible in every frame.
Several country names are clipped by neighbouring cards, reading Norw, Gree or just ia.
polish_why: Tactile drag and tilt; clipped labels and an invisible headline make the demo look unfinished.
title: Draggable Card
